candidate.name: compact_read_annotator
candidate.hypothesis: Appending a compact, delimited, factual state digest to successful read-tool results (variant option/availability/price table for product and item lookups; item plus payment-history table plus owner payment methods for order lookups; payment-method table with balances for user lookups) will let the small solver map requested option combinations to the correct item id and payment method id without parsing multi-kilobyte JSON, converting some of the 7 db0/nl1 tasks that executed a write with wrong item/variant/payment arguments and lifting accuracy from 0.38 to about 0.42-0.46, because the dominant failure cell (21 of 31 failures) is a wrong final DB state with a correct policy conversation.
candidate.changes: New plugin agents/compact_read_annotator.py exporting register() and identity AgentHarness. register() monkeypatches use_tool on the plain tau2 retail Tools class (tau2 imported lazily inside the installer, whole install wrapped in try/except). On the success path only, the wrapper appends a delimited digest built purely from the current DB to the serialized result of four read tools (get_product_details, get_item_details, get_order_details, get_user_details): one line per variant with item id, availability, price and option key=value pairs (available first, unavailable capped); order status, item lines, payment-history lines and the owning user's payment methods with gift-card balance or card brand/last4; user payment methods. Digest is ASCII, capped at 1200 chars with tail truncation, skipped when a product has fewer than 3 variants. Write tools, list/find/calculate and transfer tools are never annotated. Original return value and type are returned unchanged whenever no digest applies, when serialization is impossible, or when any extraction step raises; tool errors propagate untouched. Class AgentHarness keeps the baseline identity surface (transform_request/transform_response).
candidate.expected_efficiency: Adds roughly 100-500 tokens per annotated read (under about 5 percent of the 6.04M-token baseline total; baseline averaged 6.7 tool calls per task), adds no extra turns or tool calls, and does not alter tool errors or DB mutations.

candidate.name: user_order_index
candidate.hypothesis: Appending a bounded user-level order index to get_user_details results (one compact line per order with order id, status, ship-to city/state/zip and leading items as name, item id, price; first six orders, first three items each, with +N markers) will let the small solver locate the order a request refers to from a single observation instead of rescanning large per-order payloads one at a time, converting several of the 10 order-identification/coverage failures among the 28 failures of the incumbent (episodes that read only 1-2 of the user's 3-6 orders before picking a target, writing on the wrong order, or stopping), and lifting accuracy from 0.44 to about 0.48-0.54, because the order-scan/coverage cell is the largest fixable failure cell and the index costs under 1.2 KB per lookup while often replacing several multi-KB order lookups.
candidate.changes: New plugin agents/user_order_index.py copied from the retained agents/compact_read_annotator.py with exactly one behavioral delta: _user_digest now appends an order index after the unchanged payment-method lines. Order ids come from user.orders, are resolved against toolkit.db.orders, missing ids are skipped, and each line renders order id, status, ship-to city/state/zip and up to three items as name/item id/price. Long product names are truncated (40 chars) and shortened further only as far as needed, computed against the existing 1200-char digest budget from an exact skeleton measurement, so up to six order ids stay visible; caps are six orders and three items per order with '+N more' / '+N more orders' markers, and the index degrades to id/status/ship lines rather than letting tail truncation hide order ids. Everything else is unchanged: the product and order digest builders, the _fit truncation, register()'s lazy import of tau2.domains.retail.tools and monkeypatch of RetailTools.use_tool (released harness flags still disabled), the success-path-only attachment with try/except fallback to the original return value, untouched error path, and the identity AgentHarness (transform_request/transform_response) surface. Module imports only stdlib json; no state, randomness, or external calls.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Adds at most about 300 characters average (<=1200 chars worst case) to each get_user_details result, while removing the need for one to three separate multi-KB get_order_details calls on order-identification episodes, so total tokens should stay flat or fall slightly; no additional turns or tool calls, and no change to tool errors or database mutations.

candidate.name: user_order_map
candidate.hypothesis: The dominant failure mechanism on the current training sample is order identification: the plain get_user_details payload exposes the user's orders only as bare ids, so the solver asks the simulated user to name the order, the user declines, and the dialog derails into escalation (17 of 26 incumbent failures ask for an order id after authenticating; 5 never read a single order). Appending a LOSSLESS bounded map of the user's orders (id, status, the order's own full ship-to street address, and every item with name/id/price) to get_user_details will convert 2-4 of those 26 failures (0.48 -> 0.52-0.56), because the same information family already converted two currently failing tasks when it was present, and the two losses mechanically attributable to that earlier bounded variant came only from its item cap (a '+1 more' marker that invited a hallucinated hidden item) and its missing street address (solver wrote a city/state/zip-only match onto the wrong order); removing both hides while keeping the method lines and all prior behavior unchanged should keep the wins and drop those regressions.
candidate.changes: New plugin agents/user_order_map.py copied from the retained agents/compact_read_annotator.py with exactly one behavioral delta: _user_digest now builds, after the unchanged payment-method lines, a full-fidelity order map derived per call from the current DB. Order ids come from user.orders in stored order, resolved against toolkit.db.orders, missing ids skipped; each line renders 'order <id> status=<status> ship=<address1[, address2], city, state, zip> items=<k> :: <name> <item_id> <price>; ...' using the order's own address and its complete item list, ASCII-flattened so one entity is one line; a leading 'orders=<total> shown=<m>' line makes any coverage gap explicit. The map is bounded by 1800 chars via a deterministic lossless-first ladder (names at 24/16/10 chars, then address2 dropped, then trailing order lines dropped with shown kept accurate; only a lone order that still cannot fit has its items replaced by an explicit '+k items (order lookup)' marker; if even that fails the map is omitted and methods-only is returned). Everything else is unchanged: the product and order digest builders and their 1200-char cap, _fit, register()'s lazy import of tau2.domains.retail.tools and monkeypatch of RetailTools.use_tool (released harness flags still disabled), success-path-only attachment with try/except fallback to the original return value, untouched error path, and the identity AgentHarness (transform_request/transform_response) surface. Module imports only stdlib json; no state, randomness, or external calls.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Adds roughly 200-800 chars per get_user_details call (hard cap 1800), on episodes that average about two such calls, i.e. well under 1.5 percent of the current ~110k tokens/task, while often replacing two to six exploratory multi-KB get_order_details reads (failures were seen reading up to six orders hunting one address), so total tokens should stay flat or fall slightly; no extra turns or tool calls, and no change to tool errors or database mutations.

candidate.name: order_payment_map
candidate.hypothesis: The residual failure cell with the clearest information gap is refund/return/settlement payment-method selection: of the incumbent's 23 failures, 5 episodes executed a write whose every other argument matched the expected final state but whose payment method was wrong or absent, and none of them ever read the individual order whose payment history carries that fact -- the user map they did read lists the user's methods but not which method paid which order, so the solver guesses (claims a card when the order was paid by gift card) or blind-retries an identical rejected call up to five times. Adding each order's original payment entry (the first payment-type history entry: method id and amount) to that order's line in the get_user_details map will let those episodes choose the recorded method from the only read they perform, converting 3-5 of the 23 failures (0.54 -> 0.60-0.64) with no change to the other failure cells, while the segment is omitted whenever the history is absent or unreadable so no passing episode can regress except through the multi-payment-method passes if the first-entry-is-original ordering assumption is wrong.
candidate.changes: New plugin agents/order_payment_map.py copied from the retained agents/user_order_map.py with exactly one behavioral delta: the per-order line of the user digest now ends with ' orig_pay=<method_id>:<amount>' built at call time from the order's payment_history entries whose transaction_type reads as 'payment' (the first entry is the original payment; a second entry is appended after a comma; further entries are summarized as ',+<k>'), amounts in the existing two-decimal format and ids ASCII-flattened. Entries of other transaction types, an absent, empty or malformed history, or any extraction failure omit the segment and leave the line byte-identical to the incumbent. The segment lives inside the unchanged 1800-char user-digest budget and the unchanged lossless-first ladder (names 24/16/10, then secondary address dropped, then trailing order lines dropped with 'shown' kept accurate); one extra final rung retries the lone-order '+k items (order lookup)' marker without the segment before the map is omitted, so no map is ever dropped just to keep a payment fact. The product digest, the order digest (which already lists payment-history lines), _fit and its 1200-char cap, register()'s lazy import and monkeypatch of RetailTools.use_tool with its wrapped-once guard and full try/except fallback to the original return value, the success-path-only attachment, the untouched error path, and the identity AgentHarness (transform_request/transform_response) surface are all unchanged; the module imports only stdlib json, keeps no state beyond the existing install guard, and makes no new calls.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Adds about 40-90 characters per order line (typically one such line per get_user_details call, and about two such calls per episode), i.e. well under 0.2 percent of the current ~110k tokens per task, and should remove repeated blind retries of rejected writes (one failing episode emitted the same invalid call five times), so total tokens should stay flat or fall slightly; no extra turns or tool calls, and no change to tool errors or database mutations.

candidate.name: refund_payment_repair
candidate.hypothesis: Of the 27 incumbent failures on the current sample, 3 end with the plain domain rejecting a return write whose payment method is neither the order's original method nor a gift card (one of them repeats the identical rejected call five times and then transfers to a human); the domain's rejection happens before any state mutation and the value its own check accepts is exactly the first entry of the order's recorded payment history, so an execution-path repair that retries the identical write once with that recorded method will convert 2 of the 3 to a DB pass (the third also requested the wrong item set) and lift sample accuracy from 0.46 to 0.50 (range 0.48-0.52). The same mechanism repaired 4 failures of the same class on the previous sample, where information-side variants (showing each order's original payment entry in the read digest) had already failed to convert them, while every call that does not raise this exact rejection stays byte-identical.
candidate.changes: New plugin agents/refund_payment_repair.py copied from the retained agents/user_order_map.py with exactly one behavioral delta, plus a new module constant and one helper. The module-level wrapper installed by register() on tau2.domains.retail.tools.RetailTools.use_tool now runs the original tool call inside try/except ValueError; when the exception message lowercased contains 'original payment method' AND the call carried both order_id and payment_method_id, it resolves the order's recorded original method directly from the live toolkit DB (db.orders[order_id].payment_history[0].payment_method_id, via the existing defensive _value/_mapping helpers, refusing anything missing, unreadable, non-string or equal to the attempted value) and retries original() exactly once with only payment_method_id substituted; if the retry raises anything, the ORIGINAL ValueError is re-raised unchanged, and on any non-matching error the original exception propagates with no retry. There is no recursion (the retry calls original, not the wrapper), no retry of any other error class, no state beyond the existing install guard, and no new imports (stdlib json only). Everything else is byte-identical to the incumbent: the product/order/user digest builders, the 1200-char and 1800-char caps and the lossless-first ladder, _fit, _serialize_result, the success-path-only digest attachment, register()'s lazy import and wrapped-once guard with full try/except fallback, and the identity AgentHarness (transform_request/transform_response) surface. No task-specific knowledge, no hardcoded ids, no evaluator access; the trigger is the domain's own public error string and the substituted value is the domain's own definition of a valid argument read from public DB state.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Zero added tokens on every call that does not raise the exact rejection (success path byte-identical) and no new tool calls or turns; on the affected episodes it collapses repeated identical rejected writes (up to five observed in one episode) to one rejection plus one repaired call, so turns and tokens on those episodes fall and the previous blind-retry loops disappear.

candidate.name: pretransfer_exhaustion_guard
candidate.hypothesis: Refusing exactly the first transfer_to_human_agents call that happens before any write has succeeded, and returning a policy-grounded message that points the solver back to the already-public lookup tools, will convert 2-4 of the 8 abandoned failures of the incumbent (episodes that escalate with zero successful writes while an information-sufficient, unexecuted tool path still existed, e.g. transferring one turn after authentication or right after the user lookup without ever reading the user's orders) into passes, lifting batch accuracy from 0.48 to 0.52-0.56, because the second transfer call always reaches the original tool unchanged so no episode can loop or lose the ability to escalate when that is genuinely correct.
candidate.changes: New plugin agents/pretransfer_exhaustion_guard.py copied from the retained agents/refund_payment_repair.py with exactly one behavioral delta inside the same single RetailTools.use_tool wrapper installed by register(): (1) whenever a call to the original tool (or to the existing repaired retry) returns without raising and the tool name is one of the seven write tools (cancel_pending_order, exchange_delivered_order_items, modify_pending_order_address, modify_pending_order_items, modify_pending_order_payment, modify_user_address, return_delivered_order_items), a per-instance boolean marker is set on the live toolkit object via getattr/setattr on self, in fail-open try/except; (2) for tool_name == 'transfer_to_human_agents', when that marker is unset and a second one-shot marker is also unset, the wrapper sets the one-shot marker and raises ValueError with one fixed, id-free guidance string (transfer not executed because nothing has been resolved yet; keep working with the available tools first, reading the user's profile/orders and the relevant order/product/item details and using a product's variant table to map the option values the user describes to an exact item id; if authentication failed, ask again for exact full name, zip code and email and retry the read-only lookups; do not tell the user they are being transferred; call transfer_to_human_agents again only if the user explicitly asks for a human agent or the request still cannot be handled after those lookups). The refusal is raised before the existing try/except, so the original tool is never called, it cannot be mistaken for a repairable original-payment rejection, and digest attachment is not reached for a refused transfer. Every later transfer reaches the original unchanged via the one-shot marker; transfers after any successful write, all non-transfer calls, and the error paths stay byte-identical. Per-instance state only (getattr/setattr on self), no module-level mutable state, no task ids or content derived from prompts, stdlib json only, same install guard / lazy tau2 import / wrapped-once attribute and the identity AgentHarness surface.
candidate.expected_efficiency: Zero token, turn or tool-call change on the 40 episodes where the guard never fires; on the roughly 10 firing episodes, one extra error tool result plus one extra assistant message (about 200-600 tokens) before the episode continues into lookups and writes it previously skipped, so total tokens should stay flat or fall as abandoned episodes turn into completed ones.
